threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal to call the Overground the 'train' instead of ‘the tube’. Everyone else has caught on by now.
Last night on the 59, a girl was singing off-key about a lost umbrella. Even the driver chuckled. Only in Brixton do we turn a bus into karaoke.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy selling handmade strudel out of a bicycle cart on Karl-Marx-Straße at 2 AM, I thought, 'Yep, this is home.'

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can catch a bus that drives straight through a park, and half the time, people just get off and walk into the grass for a picnic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they navigate BART delays; they're the ones casually rolling with the punches while tourists panic at the station.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling while waiting for the 14 to arrive. The Muni bus pulled up just as he dropped his last ball. Classic San Francisco timing.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Many tourists think all the locals hang out at Parc Güell, but really, we're at the corner bars sipping vermut and watching the world go by.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always spot them by the way they clutch their metro ticket like it’s a golden ticket, nervous about getting the wrong train.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 106 bus is the quickest way to get to Dalston. We all know it's a trap during rush hour.
Heard a guy at the back of the 35 bragging he once paid a fiver for a two pints 'happy hour' in a pub that doesn't exist anymore. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw the kebab shop owner personally delivering food on a bicycle, weaving through traffic, I knew Neukölln had its own rhythm.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a bar where the bathroom has a vending machine for pinky rings. It's a quirky blend of fashion and function that perfectly captures the city's spirit.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: If they know to avoid the Civic Center BART station after a loud bang, they're probably a local. Tourists are still figuring out the system.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus the other night—driver turned the lights down low and played smooth jazz. Felt like a private concert on wheels amid the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the local bars serve tapas. Most actually serve 'platillos', and they’re usually a lot heartier than what you’d see in a guidebook.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their constant Google Maps checking at every corner, looking lost even when they’re two steps from the metro.
